rows.R: Main p1 abstract and p3 Results print the surgery HbA1c change as 1.6% with 95% CI -1.8% to -1.3% (point outside its interval) and the medical change as 0.2% (-0.5% to 0.2%); Table 2 p6 gives signed -1.6 and -0.2 with the same CIs. Mixed sign convention; direction is clear from 'decreased' and Table 2.
rows.evidence: Main article PDF p1, p3 (text layer), p6 Table 2 (rendered at 130 dpi and viewed). Card C001 read after judgment; it agrees.
rows.rationale: Prose gives unsigned decrease magnitudes alongside signed-change CIs. Literal +1.6 lies outside [-1.8,-1.3]; Table 2 gives -1.6 inside. The medical +0.2 equals the upper limit while the table gives -0.2. Not a rounding matter. The intended meaning (a decrease) is clear from wording and Table 2, so I rate it minor presentation; an extractor taking the prose value could pair a positive point with a negative interval, hence J possible.

rows.R: Year-12 HbA1c difference -1.1% (-1.7 to -0.5) is given P=.002 in main p1/p3 but P<.001 in eTable 2 (supp 2 p15), same model and interval. Wald P from the CI = .0003 (worst-case rounding .0015); the two printed P values conflict; inference unchanged.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1, p3 (text); Supplement 2 p15 eTable 2 (rendered, viewed), p4-5 methods (text). Card C002 read afterwards; agrees.
rows.rationale: Same contrast, outcome, year, estimate and CI in both documents; P values .002 vs <.001 cannot both be correct. R: se=(-0.5-(-1.7))/(2*1.96)=0.306; z=3.59; two-sided P=0.00033; with extreme rounding (est -1.05, CI -1.75 to -0.45) P=0.0015. The CI favors <.001 but a Satterthwaite/t-based contrast could give a larger P. Either way the contrast is significant and the interval is identical, so minor presentation; P values are rarely extracted.

rows.R: Abstract p1: '4 deaths (2.2%), 2 in each group' with N=262 enrolled; 4/262 = 1.5%. Table 3 p8 arm values 2/96=2.1% and 2/166=1.2% reproduce. No alternative denominator is stated. Counts are correct, so the percentage alone is wrong.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1, p3, p7 death paragraph, p8 Table 3 (text layer). Card C003 read afterwards; agrees.
rows.rationale: R: 100*4/262 = 1.53%; 2/96 = 2.08%; 2/166 = 1.20%. 2.2% does not correspond to any stated denominator (4/182 would be needed). Counts and arm-level percentages are correct and are what would be extracted, so minor presentation, J unlikely.

rows.R: Protocol v6 p17, p26-27, p29 define the primary outcome as relative percent change in HbA1c (power assumes -15% vs -7% to +2%); the report's Table 2 footnote b (p6) and eTable 2 present net (absolute) change in HbA1c units (-1.4 points), while main p2 still calls it 'percent change'.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 (protocol v6, 15APR2020) p17, p26-29 (text); main PDF p2, p6 (rendered); supplement 2 p4, p15. Card C004 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Plan response Y = percent change of HbA1c from baseline; reported values (8.2 to 8.0, change -0.2; 8.7 to 7.2, change -1.6) are absolute differences in percentage points, explicitly labeled 'net change' in Table 2 footnote b, distinct from 'relative changes' used for other outcomes. This is a change of outcome scale for the primary endpoint. The main-text Methods wording also conflicts with the table footnote, an additional report-internal inconsistency.

rows.R: Protocol p18 and Table A1 p29 define remission as HbA1c <6.5% off diabetes medications with no duration; main p2 requires no medications for at least 3 months, assessed annually. The report adds an operational window; threshold and medication criterion agree.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p18, p29 (text); main PDF p1, p2, p6, p7 Figure 3 caption (text). Card C005 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: A real difference in the written definition (3-month medication-free requirement added). It is an operational specification of the same construct; the plan defers detailed algorithms to a Manual of Operations not supplied. I describe it as minor rather than substantive because the threshold and the off-medication criterion are unchanged and an annual assessment would rarely be affected, but the count of remitters could differ in principle.

rows.R: Protocol Table A1 p30 lists major adverse cardiovascular events under Aim 2 Safety (vascular efficacy outcomes are stroke, retinopathy, nephropathy, foot ulcer); main p2 lists major adverse cardiovascular events among 'other secondary outcomes'. Plan p18 says some study outcomes are also secondary endpoints without naming them.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p18, p29-30 (text); main PDF p1, p2, p8 Table 3 (text). Card C006 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Outcome-status difference (safety in plan, secondary in report). The plan's generic statement that some study outcomes are also secondary endpoints could cover it, so the extent of the change cannot be settled; L indeterminate.

rows.R: Planned primary model A1 (protocol p26) adjusts for group, visit, group x visit and site only; baseline HbA1c appears among further sensitivity covariates (p34). The reported primary model (main p2-3; supp 2 p4) includes baseline HbA1c as a fixed effect.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p26-27, p34 (text); main PDF p2-3; supplement 2 p4 (text). Card C007 read afterwards; agrees.
rows.rationale: Covariate set of the primary analysis differs from the plan: baseline HbA1c moved from a planned sensitivity analysis into the primary model. Not disclosed as a change in the report. Describes a difference in the primary analysis model.

rows.R: Planned sensitivity analyses (protocol p30-31, p34: MICE with Rubin's rules, pattern-mixture models, MSM with combined treatment and censoring weights, per-protocol discarding post-crossover outcomes, expanded baseline-covariate models) are not reported; the report gives only an IPW per-protocol analysis with treatment weights (main p3; supp 2 p5).
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p30-31, p34 (text); main PDF p3, p9 limitations; supplement 2 p4-6, p9 (text). Searched both report documents for imputation, pattern mixture, censoring weight. Card C008 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: No multiple-imputation, pattern-mixture, outcome-discard per-protocol or expanded-covariate results are present in the main article or supplement 2. The reported IPW analysis reassigns post-crossover treatment rather than discarding outcomes and describes no censoring weight. Planned sensitivity analyses of the primary outcome not reported.

rows.R: Plan model A2 (protocol p27) is a mixed-effects logistic model with a patient random intercept for glycemic control and remission; the report (main p3; supp 2 p4) analyzes these outcomes with GEE and sandwich SEs, adjusting for baseline HbA1c. No A2 result is reported.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p27 (text); main PDF p3, p6 Table 2; supplement 2 p4-5, p15 (text). Card C009 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Model family changed from conditional (GLMM) to marginal (GEE) for the key binary secondary outcomes, which also changes the estimand of the odds ratios; covariate set also extended to baseline HbA1c. Not disclosed as a change.

rows.R: Table 2 p6, medical group change OR for diabetes medication use 0.10 (0.01 to 3.27): geometric CI midpoint 0.18 (rounding range 0.128-0.222), while all 17 other OR cells in the table reproduce sqrt(L*U) within rounding. Point or a limit likely misprinted; within-group change, not the group comparison.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p6 Table 2 (rendered and viewed); supplement 2 p4 GEE/sandwich method (text). Card C010 read afterwards; same computation.
rows.rationale: R: sqrt(0.01*3.27)=0.181; with half-unit rounding [sqrt(0.005*3.265), sqrt(0.015*3.275)] = [0.128, 0.222]; printed 0.10 is outside. Other cells: e.g., 3.39 vs mid 3.386; 0.09 vs 0.085; 0.53 vs 0.530; 6.42 vs 6.433. GEE sandwich Wald intervals are log-symmetric, so one value in this cell is likely wrong; probable rather than confirmed because the cell-specific interval method is not stated and near-boundary proportions (99% at baseline) might have been handled differently. The between-group OR 0.09 (0.03-0.24) reproduces, so interpretation is unaffected.

rows.R: Plan p34 specifies Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (site-stratified) tests for microvascular/macrovascular and safety outcomes; supp 2 p6 and eTable 5/6 footnotes state chi-squared or Fisher exact tests, with no stratification mentioned.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p26, p34-35 (text); supplement 2 p6, p17-21 (text); main PDF p1, p7. Card C011 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Different test for event outcomes: site-stratified CMH planned versus unstratified chi-squared/Fisher reported. The report's 'chi-squared' could in principle denote CMH, but no strata are mentioned, so the plain reading is a change of test. These are descriptive safety comparisons with small counts.

rows.R: Within the protocol, model A1 (p26) treats site as fixed (Z site vector and b_i 'fixed effect for site'), but the power section (p28) uses a fitted site variance component sigma_b=0.06 and p31 describes site effects as following a distribution with the CI reflecting heterogeneity. The operative fixed-site specification is clear and matches the report.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p26-28, p31 (text); main PDF p2-3; supplement 2 p4 (text). Card C012 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Real inconsistency in how site heterogeneity is described (fixed vs random site). Also A1 includes both Z and b_i for site, relying on an identifiability clause (p27). Because the analysis specification itself states fixed site, the conflict mainly affects the description of the power simulation and the heterogeneity interpretation, not the analysis; I rate it minor.

rows.R: Protocol Appendix 2 (p55-56): randomized 155+69+43+45+43=355, underwent intervention 154+61+38+40+32=325 (also p27), implying 30 not treated, but the dagger footnote says 38 dropped at randomization. Background participant accounting; the 302 eligible figure (140+56+35+39+32) is unaffected.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p27, p55-56 (text layer; table read column by column). Card C013 read afterwards; same sums.
rows.rationale: Arithmetic: 355-325=30 vs stated 38. Column checks: 154-2-12=140, 61-0-5=56, 38-0-3=35, 40-1-0=39, 32=32, total 302, consistent with the sample-size basis on p28. The inconsistency concerns historical enrollment description, not the analysis design; minor. Note the published report gives yet another count (39 withdrew before intervention; 316 eligible), likely a later data snapshot.

rows.R: eTable 1 (supp 2 p14), 7-year column N=262: Other race 4 (1.9); 4/262=1.5%. Race counts 81+176+4=261, not 262; main Table 1 gives White 59+118=177 (67.6%) and Other 2+2=4, whereas eTable 1 and the abstract give White 176 (67.2%).
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p14 eTable 1 (rendered, viewed); main PDF p1, p3, p4 Table 1 (text). Card C014 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: R: 4/262=1.53%, 5/262=1.91%, 176/262=67.18%, 177/262=67.56%. The printed 1.9% matches 5/262, so either the Other count or White count is off by one; main Table 1 arms sum to 177 White and 4 Other. Descriptive baseline row; minor presentation. The White 176 vs 177 discrepancy (abstract 67.2% vs Table 1 counts) is a related issue outside this candidate.

rows.R: Main p4: follow-up imaging was MRI in 8 of 336 (2%) and CT in 328 (98%); p9 and eTable 11 (supp 5 p51; N 101+24+79=204) describe 204 (61%) patients with MR diffusion follow-up; p11 says 'two-thirds'. The count of the post hoc infarct-growth population is irreconcilable within the report.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p4, p6, p9, p11 (text layer); supplement 5 p51 eTable 11 (text). Card C001 read afterwards; agrees.
rows.rationale: 8/336=2.4% vs 204/336=60.7%; 101+24+79=204. The 8 most likely refers to baseline MRI selection (p6: 'excluding 8 patients who received MRI'), carried into a follow-up statement, but the report does not say so. The denominator of the infarct-growth analysis and the follow-up modality mix are thereby ambiguous; also p11 'two-thirds' does not match 61%. Separately, p9 gives MM infarct growth IQR 56-125 mL whereas eTable 11 gives 56-135 mL (outside this candidate).

rows.R: Analysis SAP (supp 4 p3, section 5.1) states all analyses will be as-treated; the report (main p4) analyzes treatment-effect comparisons across imaging strata by randomized group and within-group associations as-treated (Figure 1; Figure 2 labeled intention to treat). Two crossovers, so numerical impact likely small.
rows.evidence: Supplement 4 p3-4 (text); main PDF p4, p6-7; supplement 5 p8 flow, p38 eTable 2 (text). Card C002 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Planned analysis population for between-arm comparisons (as-treated) differs from the reported one (randomized group). 168 randomized EVT vs 170 as-treated EVT; 168/166 vs 170/166. Not disclosed as a change.

rows.R: Analysis SAP p3 makes composite core (larger of CTP/MRI and CT hypodensity) the primary volume and CTP/MRI core a sensitivity analysis; the appendix (p7) calls composite core pre-specified. The report uses CTP/MRI core as the main measure and labels composite-core analyses post hoc (main p4, p6; Figure 3; eFigure 10).
rows.evidence: Supplement 4 p3, p7 (text); main PDF p1, p4, p6, p8, p11 (text); supplement 5 p16. Card C003 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: The primary/sensitivity hierarchy of the core-volume measure is reversed, and a planned analysis is described as post hoc. This changes which estimates are the headline results (abstract reports CTP/MRI core strata).

rows.R: eFigures 7 and 8 (supp 5 p13-14): ASPECTS 0-2 (n=19) has 0 events in both arms for mRS 0-2 and for mRS 0-3, yet both print RR 1.00 (0.37-2.72), identical across outcomes; other zero-cell rows (e.g., >=150 mL) print '*'. A risk ratio is not estimable with no events in either arm.
rows.evidence: Supplement 5 p13-14 eFigures 7-8 (rendered at 110 dpi, viewed); supplement 4 p4-5 (modified Poisson plan); main PDF p4. Card C004 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: With 0/n vs 0/n, the modified Poisson MLE does not exist; a finite RR with a finite CI, identical for two outcomes, looks like a placeholder or artifact. The same figures use '*' for other non-estimable rows, so the display rule is inconsistent. A reader or meta-analyst could extract RR 1.00 (0.37-2.72) for the ASPECTS 0-2 subgroup, and it may enter the interaction P (.9055/.6788).

rows.R: Main p6/abstract (aGenOR 0.91, 0.82-1.00, 'significantly worse') and p10 (aRR 0.97, 0.93-1.00, 'significantly decreased'): upper limits print as 1.00 at two decimals; unrounded limits in [0.995, 1.000) are compatible with the significance statements. No P values are given that would contradict them. Rounding explains the apparent conflict.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1, p6, p7 Table 2 (rendered), p10 (rendered). Card C005 read afterwards; it retains the case under a category rule despite rounding.
rows.rationale: A printed bound of 1.00 cannot establish that the interval includes 1; e.g., 0.996 rounds to 1.00. The same paragraph describes aRR 1.00 (0.99-1.00) as non-significant, which is likewise compatible with an unrounded upper bound above 1. Reporting a third decimal would have been better, but there is no demonstrable error.

rows.R: Figure 2B (main p7, core >=100 mL): segment colors assign EVT 2/6/10/20 to mRS 0-3 (no mRS 4 segment), giving mRS 0-2 18% and 0-3 38%; eFigures 7-8 give 4/51 (7.8%) and 9/51 (17.6%), and the Discussion says about 80% had mRS >=4. The values fit if each segment is shifted one category (mRS 1-6); MM bar shows the same shift.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p7 Figure 2 (rendered at 300 dpi crop, colors checked against legend), p10 Discussion (rendered); supplement 5 p13-14 eFigures 7-8 (rendered). Card C006 read afterwards; agrees.
rows.rationale: EVT segments 2,6,10,20,10,53 colored mRS 0,1,2,3,5,6: 0-2 = 18%, 0-3 = 38% vs 4/51=7.84%, 9/51=17.65%. Reading the segments as mRS 1..6 gives 0-2 = 8%, 0-3 = 18%, >=4 = 83%, matching the supplement and Discussion. MM (2,4,16,16,61 colored mRS 0,2,3,5,6) gives 0-2 6%, 0-3 22% vs 1/49=2.0%, 3/49=6.1%; reading as mRS 2..6 gives 2% and 6%. Panel A reproduces the eFigure counts (EVT 0-2 26% vs 30/117=25.6%). The primary-outcome distribution of a key subgroup is misdisplayed.

rows.R: Main p8 states that as mismatch volume increased the marginal probability of mRS 0-2 and 0-3 increased with EVT and decreased with MM; eFigure 17A/B (supp 5 p23) shows both EVT curves (and MM curves) decreasing across mismatch volume.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p8 (text); supplement 5 p23 eFigure 17 (rendered, viewed). Card C007 read afterwards; agrees.
rows.rationale: Direct visual check: EVT mRS 0-2 falls from about 0.26 at -100 mL to about 0.05 at 380 mL; mRS 0-3 from about 0.63 to 0.07; MM curves also fall. The narrative direction contradicts the cited figure. Because the text uses this to argue for mismatch-related benefit with EVT, the error bears on interpretation.

rows.R: E changed: the issue is which core variable conditions the age/time surfaces, a labeling conflict rather than a numerical error. eFigure 18 title says CTP/MRI core while its explanation says composite core; eFigure 19 uses composite core; main p10 cites both and says 'consistent across estimated CT perfusion/MRI core volumes'.
rows.evidence: Supplement 5 p24-25 eFigures 18-19 (rendered, viewed); main PDF p3, p10 (rendered). Card C008 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Real labeling inconsistency. The eFigure 18 explanation appears to be copied from eFigure 19, and the title plus main text indicate CTP/MRI core for eFigure 18; the surfaces are illustrative point predictions without intervals, so I rate it minor. If the composite core was in fact used, the 70/100/150 mL settings would mean different patients.

rows.R: Analysis SAP p5 (section 5.2.3) plans predicted probabilities of independent ambulation by age and time from last known well to randomization in EVT patients; the report shows age by time from CTP to reperfusion/end of procedure (eFigure 18) and from LKW to reperfusion/end of procedure (eFigure 19). No LKW-to-randomization surface is reported.
rows.evidence: Supplement 4 p5 (text); main PDF p10; supplement 5 p24-25 (rendered). Card C009 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: The time predictor differs from the planned one (different time intervals with different end points), and the planned surface is absent. Not disclosed.

rows.R: Protocol (Aug 2021) synopsis p8 and section 3.7.1.1 p37 call mRS 0-2 the second primary outcome, but protocol p50 calls it 'our secondary endpoint'; the trial SAP v1.0.0 (Nov 2022, p13, p17) lists it as secondary. Infarct volume/lesion growth are secondary in protocol p50 but tertiary in SAP p13.
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p8, p37, p50 (text); supplement 3 p13, p14, p17 (scanned; OCR at 250 dpi). Card C010 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Outcome hierarchy conflicts within the protocol itself and between protocol and SAP. The later SAP resolves it as secondary, which this report follows, but the protocol's internal conflict concerns a design element (primary vs secondary status).

rows.R: Protocol p13 background: results of the earlier non-randomized SELECT cohort (aOR 2.92, 1.00-7.91, P=.041; 2.01, 1.00-4.03, P=.049). Background literature, not a design element of SELECT2 or this analysis; the 1.00 lower limits are also compatible with rounding.
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p13 (text). Card C011 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Historical results quoted in a protocol rationale do not affect the planned design or the reported analysis. In addition, unrounded lower limits in (1.000, 1.005) would agree with P<.05, so no inconsistency is demonstrated.

rows.R: Protocol p14 background: SELECT cohort safety outcomes 'significantly increased' include sICH 8/173 vs 3/18, P=.072. A wording slip in the historical rationale, not a design element of this trial or analysis.
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p14 (text). Card C012 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: 8/173=4.6% and 3/18=16.7% reproduce the printed 5% and 17%. Describing P=.072 as significant is loose wording about prior-study results; it does not bear on the SELECT2 design or this report.

rows.R: Protocol Appendix B (p80-81) and trial SAP (p39-40): W is the rank sum of mRS scores in the EVT group and efficacy is claimed if Z >= b; H_A is P(Y <= X) = 1/2 + theta with Y = MM and X = EVT mRS. As written, large values indicate worse (higher) EVT mRS, opposite to benefit (lower mRS, p37).
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p37, p80-81 (text); supplement 3 p39-40 (scanned; OCR at 250 dpi, formulas partly garbled, checked against protocol text). Card C013 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Orientation of the efficacy statistic is inverted relative to the clinical direction. Intended meaning (efficacy favoring EVT) is clear from context and the decision was evidently implemented in the beneficial direction, so I treat this as a notational inconsistency (descending ranks or reversed X/Y would resolve it) rather than a substantive design conflict.

rows.R: Trial SAP section 7.2 (p9) and Appendix B (p40) prespecify interim looks at 200 and 380 patients; section 7.5 (p12) says the DSMB 300-patient review was provided 'without making any alteration to the study design or incorporating any additional interim analyses', yet the trial was stopped because the efficacy boundary was crossed at 300 using 'pre-specified boundaries'. The boundary applicable at 300 is not specified.
rows.evidence: Supplement 3 p9, p11-12, p40 (scanned; OCR at 250 dpi; p12 rendered at 140 dpi because OCR dropped the watermark-overlaid sentence on design alteration). Main PDF p4. Card C014 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: The SAP simultaneously denies an additional interim analysis and reports a formal efficacy decision at an unscheduled information time. Which boundary (b = 2.604 for the planned looks or an adjusted one) was applied, and how type I error was controlled, cannot be determined. This concerns the stopping decision the report cites (main p4).

rows.R: Analysis SAP p5 (5.2.5) defines sICH with a >=4-point NIHSS increase 'at 4-hour follow-up window' and no death component; trial SAP p13 uses '>=4-point increase ... or death within 24 hours' and p18/p31 a 24-hour window. Report cites SITS-MOST and reports counts only.
rows.evidence: Supplement 4 p5 (text); supplement 3 p13, p18, p31 (scanned; OCR). Main PDF p3; supplement 5 p38. Card C015 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Two plan documents give different sICH definitions (4 h vs 24 h; death included vs not). The 4-hour window is very likely a typographic slip for 24 hours, and sICH is only tabulated descriptively in this analysis, so the intended definition (SITS-MOST) is reasonably clear; the death component difference could in principle change counts.

rows.R: Analysis SAP p6 (5.3.3) plans stratification by mismatch volume thresholds of 50 and 100 mL; neither the main article nor supplement 5 reports these strata (only the two ratio/volume mismatch profiles and a continuous mismatch-volume analysis, eFigure 17).
rows.evidence: Supplement 4 p4, p6 (text); searched the full text of the main PDF and supplement 5 (all 53 pages) for mismatch-volume thresholds; main p6, p8; supplement 5 p23, p43. Card C016 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Planned subgroup analysis not reported. The continuous analysis is related but is not the planned categorical stratification.

rows.R: eFigure 13 (supp 5 p19), RR of mRS 5-6 (adverse) with EVT vs MM: all 16 RRs are below 1 (favoring EVT), but the axis labels read 'Favours Medical Management' on the left and 'Favours Thrombectomy' on the right. eFigure 9 (p15), the same outcome, labels the axis correctly.
rows.evidence: Supplement 5 p15 and p19 (rendered at 110 dpi, viewed). Card C017 read afterwards; agrees.
rows.rationale: Reversed direction labels on an adverse-outcome forest plot. Numbers, caption and the parallel eFigure 9 make the correct direction recoverable, so presentation-level, but a reader relying on the labels would invert the conclusion.

rows.R: Discordant profile 2 (ASPECTS 6-10, core >=70 mL): eTable 9 MM has mRS 0-3 3/11 and mRS 5-6 10/11 (13 > 11); eTable 10 MM has 4/12 and 11/12 (15 > 12) and mRS 0-2 2/12 with 11/12. eTable 8 attributes the favorable counts to EVT (mRS 0-2 1/12, 0-3 3/12; MM 0/11), so arms appear swapped for favorable outcomes in eTables 9-10.
rows.evidence: Supplement 5 p45-50 eTables 8-10 (text layer, row by row). Card C018 read afterwards; agrees (I did not separately inspect eFigure 20 on p31-32).
rows.rationale: Disjoint categories cannot sum above the denominator: 3+10=13>11; 4+11=15>12; 2+11=13>12. eTable 8 sums are coherent (EVT 75+76+12=163; MM 82+63+11=156; outcome counts sum to row totals: e.g., mRS 0-2 EVT 10+21+1=32). The as-treated vs ITT difference (one crossover in the concordant row) cannot move favorable outcomes between arms in profile 2 where denominators are equal (12/11). Extractable subgroup counts are wrong in eTables 9-10, and the N/A labels hide a non-zero MM count.

rows.R: Protocol (Aug 2021) p48: at the final analysis, if the overall efficacy bound is not crossed, an optimal subgroup is selected and tested; trial SAP v1.0.0 (Nov 2022) p10: if the final efficacy bound is not crossed, EVT is declared not superior (no subgroup rescue). The final stage was never reached (trial stopped at the 300-patient review).
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p1, p45-49, p81 (text); supplement 3 p2, p9-10, p12, p40 (scanned; OCR). Card C019 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: The decision rules at the final analysis differ between plan versions; a final-stage subgroup test after overall failure changes the testing procedure and error allocation. The later SAP likely supersedes, but neither document records the change. No effect on the reported analysis because the final stage was not reached.

rows.R: Protocol p5 primary analysis: logistic regression with 'all estimates adjusted for baseline confounders'; report p4 uses ordinary logistic regression with no covariates named, and Table 2 RR 1.35 (1.17-1.57) and OR 1.57 reproduce the crude 287/759 vs 208/744 exactly. The primary estimates appear unadjusted.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 (protocol) p5-6, p15 summary of changes (text); main PDF p1, p4-6 Table 2 (text); supplement 2 p14 eTable 5 (rendered). Card C001 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: R: RR=(287/759)/(208/744)=1.3525, log-Wald CI 1.168-1.567; OR=(287*536)/(472*208)=1.567. These match the printed unadjusted values. The protocol's adjustment commitment is not implemented or not described; the summary of protocol changes (p15) does not mention it. Difference in the primary analysis model (unadjusted vs adjusted); in a randomized trial the numerical consequence is likely small.

rows.R: Main p2 says the waitlist group was not included in tests of statistical significance; p4 reports retention P=.02 (1 month) and P=.11 (7 months). These reproduce only as 3-group chi-square tests including waitlist (P=.017, .115); the 2-group tests give P=.009 and .073. Conclusions about retention are unchanged.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p2, p4, p6 Figure (text). Recomputed in R. Card C002 read afterwards; same 3-group values.
rows.rationale: R chisq.test on responders/nonresponders: 1 month 609/759, 636/744, 152/178 gives P=0.0173 (3 groups) vs 0.0086 (2 groups, Yates) or 0.0070 (no correction); 7 months 521/759, 543/744, 132/178 gives P=0.1149 vs 0.0729 or 0.0643. The printed P values correspond to the 3-group test, contradicting the stated exclusion of the waitlist group from significance testing. Retention tests are descriptive; significance classification is unchanged.

rows.R: E changed: main article p3 says participants who set a quit date receive messages 6 weeks before and 8 weeks after it; the results supplement eAppendix A (supp 2 p2) says 1 week before and 8 weeks after, as does the protocol (p2). The plan only corroborates the supplement, so this is a report-internal conflict about the intervention.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p3 (text); supplement 2 p2 eAppendix A (text); supplement 1 p2, p4, p15 (text). Card C003 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Six vs one week of prequit messaging is a material difference in the described intervention (total program length 14 vs 9 weeks for quit-date setters). Possibly the main text describes a later program version, but nothing says so. Not a statistical design element, hence not protocol_report; the conflict sits between two report documents.

rows.R: Protocol p5-6: identify potential moderators (e.g., age, gender, motivation) and examine treatment-by-moderator interactions for those associated with the primary outcome; report p4-5 and eAppendix D/eTable 6 test every Table 1 characteristic one at a time with Holm adjustment across about 25 tests.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p5-6, p15 (text); main PDF p4-5 (text); supplement 2 p6, p15 (text). Card C004 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: The moderator family and selection rule differ: a screened subset with interaction models in the plan versus all baseline characteristics with Holm multiplicity control in the report. No planned association screen is reported. Exploratory analysis in both; the difference affects which tests were done and the multiplicity family.

rows.R: eTable 5 (supp 2 p14), 30-day IPRW OR 1.92 (1.50, 2.24): a log-symmetric interval with lower 1.50 implies an upper limit near 2.46 (1.92^2/1.50); all 11 other RR/OR cells in the table are log-symmetric within rounding. rows.R: Both SAP versions (p142 lines 2387-2389; p162 lines 2803-2805) specify Fisher exact tests for grouped AEs; Table S11 (supp 1 p24) footnotes label overall, nervous-system and disabling-stroke rows as chi-square. rows.rationale: R fisher.test/chisq.test on 12/249 vs 14/252, 7/249 vs 12/252, 6/249 vs 18/252. Overall: Fisher .8409, Yates .8650, Pearson .7103; nervous: .3501, .3634, .2531; disabling: .0196, .0231, .0131. rows.R: Original protocol synopsis (supp 2 p11-12): 686 patients, 91 endpoint events, '90% confidence', Lan-DeMets; section 20.1 (p40-41): 686 patients, 80% power, O'Brien-Fleming. With 12.76% vs 6.25% one-year risk and 1:1 allocation, 686 patients give about 65 first-year events, and the required events are about 56 (80%) or 75 (90%). The 91-event figure does not reproduce; the design was later re-estimated to 512.
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p11-12, p18, p40-41, p126 (text); main PDF p3. Computed in R. Card C007 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: R: HR=log(1-0.0625)/log(1-0.1276)=0.473; Schoenfeld events 4(z.975+z_power)^2/log(HR)^2 = 55.9 (80%) and 74.9 (90%), x1.06 = 59.3 and 79.4; expected events 343*0.1276+343*0.0625 = 65.2. The original protocol also conflicts internally on power (90% vs 80%) and spending function. What 91 represents (required events under other assumptions, longer horizon) cannot be determined, and the original design was superseded by the 512-patient amendment used in the report, so I leave K indeterminate.

rows.R: Table 3 (main p9) ED visits: absolute difference 3.38 (95% CrI -0.57 to 7.94) vs rate ratio 1.72 (1.03-2.87), P=.04. Different models and inferential summaries; no contradiction.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1, p4, p6, p9 Table 3 and footnote b (rendered); supplement 2 p17 eTable 12 (rendered). Card C001 read afterwards; it notes the same model difference.

The report attributes significance to the rate ratio from the prespecified Poisson model, consistent with P=.04 and the CI 1.03-2.87. Showing a less-adjusted Bayesian absolute difference beside it invites confusion, but the footnote discloses it.

rows.R: Protocol (supp 1 p11) and SAP (p36) specify that if residuals of the primary model are substantially non-normal, two sensitivity analyses will be done: a normalizing transformation and an ordinal regression. eFigure 1 (supp 2 p18) reports residuals 'clearly non-normal' and gives only the square-root transformation; no ordinal model of the total score is reported in the main article or supplement 2.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p11, p31, p36 (text); main PDF p3-4; supplement 2 p18-19 (text); searched both report documents for 'ordinal' and 'transform'. Card C002 read afterwards.

rows.R: Final protocol item 5 (supp 1 p12) and SAP (p37): intervention outcomes analyzed as simple differences in proportions ignoring clustering, Fisher exact P values and Newcombe CIs. rows.R: eTable 10 (supp 2 p13-14), mouth sores among SSPedi>=3: symptom screening 0/0 (empty), yet finite ORs are printed: 2.6 (0.04-170.4), 5.00 (0.07-366.4) twice. These equal Haldane 0.5-corrected crude ORs ((0.5x6.5)/(0.5x2.5)=2.6; (0.5x7.5)/(0.5x1.5)=5.0), a method not described; a comparison with an empty group is not estimable.

With zero participants in one arm there is no information, so any OR is an artifact of the correction. The intervals are uninformative and P>.99, so interpretation is unaffected; presentation and method-description problem.

rows.R: eTable 10 sadness, any intervention, all participants: OR 0.51 (0.26-0.99), P=.05, called significant (main p5) under the P<.05 rule. The CI implies P about .048, which rounds to .05 and is below .05. Consistent once rounding is considered.
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p13 (rendered); main PDF p4-5 (text). Recomputed in R. Card C006 read afterwards; it keeps the case under a category rule.
rows.rationale: R: SE=(ln 0.99 - ln 0.26)/3.92 = 0.341; z = ln 0.51/0.341 = -1.97; P = 0.048. Printed .05 is the two-decimal rounding of a value below .05, and the interval excludes 1. No inconsistency; a three-decimal P would have avoided the ambiguity.

rows.R: eTable 10 symptom-specific intervention, SSPedi>=1: neuropathy 6/57 vs 0/70, OR 17.8 (0.98-323.1), P=.007; hunger 6/111 vs 0/130, OR 16.08 (0.9-288.74), P=.009; main p6 calls both significant. CI and P come from different, undisclosed methods.
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p14-15 (rendered), p22 eMethods (text); main PDF p4-6 (text). Recomputed in R. Card C007 read afterwards; the card did not identify the methods; my Fisher/Haldane reproduction goes beyond it.
rows.rationale: R: Haldane OR for 6/57 vs 0/70 = 17.80 (0.98, 323.06); Fisher P = 0.00702; for 6/111 vs 0/130: 16.08 (0.90, 288.74), Fisher P = 0.00886. Each row pairs a CI that includes 1 with a P<.01, under a footnote naming logistic regression, which cannot give finite estimates with a zero cell. Fisher's test is a reasonable choice for sparse data, so the significance claim is defensible, but the reporting is internally contradictory and the methods are misdescribed.

rows.R: Abstract (main p1): 'Among the 338 randomized infants ..., 320 underwent operative repair'. Figure 1 (p3) and text (p4-5) give 152 early (147+5) and 129 late (90+39) repairs = 281; 320 is the number remaining after withdrawals (163+157), the population described in Table 1.

The abstract attributes demographic summaries to 'operative repair' infants and overstates the number repaired by 39 (12%). In a trial of repair timing, the number actually repaired is a key process measure; an extractor would take 320 as repaired.

rows.R: Protocol v7 p13: primary outcome by binomial GLMM with log link; hospital days by a lognormal model. Report p4: logistic mixed model (Bayesian), but frequentist primary by GEE logistic due to nonconvergence (disclosed), and negative binomial mixed model for hospital days.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p13 lines 471-488 (text); supplement 2 p7-8 lines 259-271 (text); main PDF p4, p6 Table 2; supplement 3 p5 eTable 2 (text). Card C002 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Model families differ across protocol, SAP and report. The report follows the later SAP for the Bayesian analysis; the frequentist GEE substitution is disclosed in the report (main p4, nonconvergence). Disclosed changes are retained as differences.

rows.R: SAP p8: prior for categorical outcomes OR 1.0 with 95% CrI 0.2-4 (Normal(0, 0.7) on log OR); count outcomes RR 95% CrI 0.33-3.3; interaction terms Normal(0, 0.6); subgroup main effects as primary. Protocol p13: RR 1.0 (0.33-3.0) and main effects N(0,1000). Report p4: OR/RR 1.0 (95% CrI 0.33-3.0) for the intervention effect and 0.33-3.0 for interactions, vague priors for other terms.

rows.rationale: R: Normal(0,0.7) gives exp(+/-1.96*0.7) = 0.25-3.94; Normal(0,0.6) gives 0.31-3.25; a 0.33-3.0 interval corresponds to SD = ln(3)/1.96 = 0.56. The prior described in the report matches the protocol rather than the final SAP for the primary binary outcome, and the description of other terms ('vague') differs from the SAP's weakly informative priors. The posterior probabilities reported (97%, 82%, 99%) depend on these priors; whether the implemented prior was the SAP or the reported one cannot be determined.

The SAP (p2) says planned analyses will appear in manuscripts 'as deemed necessary', and the 2-year neurodevelopmental outcome is explicitly deferred, but the per-protocol primary analysis and the planned modifiers belong to the primary-outcome report.

rows.R: Abstract (p1) and Results (p5) state no significant difference in any of the 11 secondary end points, but Table 2 (p6) gives EQ-5D-5L postoperative day 5 difference -0.057 (95% CI -0.111 to -0.003), P=.04, favoring placebo. The SAP (p14) specifies no multiplicity adjustment and time-point effects from the time-by-treatment model.

Under the planned unadjusted time-point analysis, one secondary contrast is nominally significant, so the summary statement is inaccurate. The difference favors placebo, so 'no benefit' remains true, and an isolated time-point result among many is weak evidence; I rate it minor. Also, PONV day 2 (5/223 vs 19/226) was not tested; a crude Fisher test gives P=.005 (outside this candidate).

rows.evidence: Supplement 1 lines 1026-1030, 2265, 2376 (text); supplement 2 p10-11 (text); main PDF p1, p4, p5, p6 (rendered). Card read afterwards.

rows.R: SAP section 11.6 (p15): sensitivity analysis comparing Edinburgh (sponsor, largest recruiter) with the other centres. Not reported in the main article or supplements 3-4.

The ERAS categories themselves were defined post hoc (supp 3 footnote), which I note but did not adjudicate.

rows.R: Subgroup eFigure (supp 3 p2): legend labels the horizontal lines '99% CI', while the caption says the numbers are 95% CIs. The plotted lines coincide with the printed numeric limits (e.g., overall 0.88-1.07; low ERAS 0.49-2.08), and the overall row equals the main 95% CI. SAP p15 specifies 99% CIs for subgroups.

Because the overall row (95%) is drawn on the same scale as the subgroup rows, the legend is more likely the error, but whether the subgroup intervals are 95% or the planned 99% cannot be determined. The interaction P values are unaffected; an extractor of subgroup CIs would not know the level.

rows.R: Abstract (p1): patients were 'randomly assigned ... restrictive (n = 733) or liberal (n = 724)' and '1979 randomized, 1508 completed the trial'. The n's labeled as randomized are analyzed counts, and 1508 did not all complete the trial.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1-3 Figure 1 (rendered, boxes traced), p5 (text). Card C001 read afterwards; same counts.
rows.rationale: 983-59-174=750, 750-17=733; 994-71-165=758, 758-34=724; 983+994+2=1979. Labeling 733/724 as randomized and 1508 as 'completed' understates post-randomization exclusion (471 of 1979, 24%) in the abstract. The abstract does give 1979, so the scale is partly recoverable; presentation-level, but the labels matter for appraising the modified ITT population.

rows.R: Protocol (supp 1 p13, p26, p49, p62): inclusion continues up to a maximum of 1600 participants and ends at 1420 evaluable participants with 30-day follow-up; SAP (p85) and report (p5): 1420 total including 3.5% dropout. Report: 1979 randomized, 1508 after secondary exclusions, 1457 analyzed.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p13, p26, p49, p62, p84-85 (text); main PDF p3, p5. Card C002 read afterwards.

The target definition also shifts (1420 evaluable vs 1420 including dropout). The plan does not define which population the cap applies to, so the difference cannot be characterized further.

rows.R: Protocol (p13, p23, p49, p59) lists 9 secondary outcomes without hierarchy; the SAP (Jan 2023, p85-89) and report (p5-6) designate death and major respiratory complications as 2 key secondary outcomes and the rest as exploratory with Benjamini-Hochberg control. Report follows the SAP.

rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p23, p26, p59, p62, p78-89 (text); main PDF p5-6 (text); supplement 2 p17. Card C007 read afterwards.

rows.R: Figure 2 (p6) and eTable 5 (supp 2 p18): SSI OR 0.50 (0.25-0.99) and adjusted OR 0.49 (0.26-0.93), P=.03, vs risk difference -3.04 (-6.87 to 0.79). Different measures from different models (stratification-adjusted OR; RD method unstated), and the report correctly states no exploratory outcome was significant after FDR control. Not a contradiction.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p5-6 Figure 2 (text), supplement 2 p18 eTable 5 (rendered), supplement 1 p86 (text). Recomputed crude RDs in R. Card C008 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: An OR and an RD from different models need not agree at the null boundary, and no significance claim is made. I note separately that the RD estimation method is not described and the printed RDs depart from crude differences more than the ORs do (e.g., SSI crude -1.29 [-3.25 to 0.66] vs printed -3.04; major respiratory complications crude -1.91 vs printed -0.61), which would merit a methods clarification but is outside this candidate's claim.

rows.R: SAP Table (supp 1 p101): SSI = purulent drainage; positive microbiology from the site AND signs of infection; or surgeon diagnosis. rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p84, p101 (text); supplement 2 p9 (rendered), p18; main PDF p6. Card C009 read afterwards.

Also 55 + 67 = 122 vs N = 130 stated (Figure 1: 59 and 71); the difference equals the 4 + 4 'omitted according to Swiss law', which the footnote does not mention.

rows.R: Protocol (supp 1 p7, p24-25, p28-30): phase 2 contrasts among week-6 nonabstainers re-randomized to continue, switch or increase. Report (p1, p4, Figure 2 p6): 40 CNRT and 35 varenicline nonabstainers who did not attend re-randomization were assigned to continuation and analyzed in it (CNRT 50+40=90; VAR 42+35=77). Disclosed in the report (p4) with a rationale; no plan provision supplied.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p7, p24-25, p28-30 (text); main PDF p1, p4, p6 Figure 2 (rendered). Card C001 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: The reference (continuation) groups in the primary contrasts include non-randomized participants who were mostly lost/nonabstinent, which can lower continuation abstinence and inflate the apparent benefit of switching or increasing. Disclosed change; still a plan-report difference in the analysis population of the primary contrasts.

rows.R: Supp 2 p5-6 defines inverse probability weights only for phase 1 abstainers (1/(0.5x1)=2) and re-randomized nonabstainers (1/(0.5x0.33)=6.06); the primary analysis also includes 75 nonabstainers assigned (not randomized) to continuation (main p4, Figure 2). Their weight and probability basis are not stated.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1, p4, p6-7 (text/rendered); supplement 2 p5-6, p19 (text). Card C002 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Arithmetic of stated weights: 2.0 and 6.06. The nonattenders' assignment probability is not 0.33; if they received 6.06 they are overweighted relative to the design, if 2.0 the continuation-cell estimate mixes two weighting schemes. The weighting of 75 of 348 nonabstainers in the primary contrasts is therefore unspecified; I cannot judge its effect on the estimates.

rows.R: Abstract (p1): CNRT 90 (47%) continued, 50 (33%) increased, 51 (34%) switched; 90/191=47% but 50/151=33% and 51/151=34% (sum 114%). Varenicline: 39 (32%) and 41 (34%) of 122, but 77 (49%) of 157. Mixed denominators within the same sentence.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1, p6 Figure 2 (rendered). Card C003 read afterwards.

rows.R: CNRT nonabstainers, switch to varenicline (or increase) vs continuation: abstract (p1) RD 6% (95% CrI 6% to 11%); Results (p5) 6% (2%-11%); eTable 4 (supp 2 p21) 6% (2%-10%) for switch and 6% (2%-11%) for increase. The abstract lower limit is wrong.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1, p5 (text); supplement 2 p21 eTable 4 (text). Card C004 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Three copies of the same contrast: lower limit 6 vs 2. A point estimate at its lower credible limit is implausible for this posterior; the body and table agree on 2%. Direction and posterior probability (>99%) unchanged; the abstract value would be extracted, hence J possible.

rows.R: Varenicline nonabstainers: switch to CNRT 0/41 (0%) vs continue 2/77 (3%). Results (p5) give RD -3% (-4% to -1%) with '>99% probability that continuing was worse than switching' (direction reversed); eTable 4 prints +3% (1% to 4%) for switch vs stay; the abstract attributes the >99% statement to 'switching to a higher dosage'. Discussion (p8) correctly describes a decrement with switching.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1, p5, p7 Figure 3, p8 (text); supplement 2 p21 eTable 4 (text). Card C005 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: 0% < 3%, so switching to CNRT was worse than continuing; the Results sentence states the opposite, eTable 4 drops the sign, and the abstract conflates this contrast with the dose-increase contrast. A key comparison's direction is misreported in two locations, which affects interpretation of a rescue strategy.

rows.R: Protocol (supp 1 p31, p33-34): a posterior probability >0.90 that the effect exists constitutes sufficient evidence, and power is described for detecting 0.90. Report (p4; supp 2 p9) states that a posterior probability >0.80 was prespecified as sufficient for confirmation.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p31, p33-34 (text, partly garbled symbols; 0.90 legible); main PDF p4; supplement 2 p8-9, p18 (text). Card C006 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: The decision threshold for the primary hypotheses differs (0.90 planned vs 0.80 reported as prespecified). With the observed >99% probabilities the conclusions would not change for most contrasts, but the 'prespecified' label is not supported by the supplied plan.

rows.R: Protocol p28 and p30: analyses with and without potential confounders, joint modeling of outcomes and missingness, pattern-mixture models for non-ignorable missingness, and sensitivity analyses with optimistic/pessimistic/skeptical priors. None is reported in the main article or supplement 2; only a post hoc dynamic treatment regime analysis is added.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p28, p30 (text); main PDF p4, p7-8; supplement 2 pp1-36 contents and text searched. Card C007 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Planned robustness analyses of the primary model (missing data, priors) are not reported. Given that missing outcomes were imputed as smoking and nonattenders were assigned to continuation, the missing-data sensitivity analyses would have been informative.

rows.R: EOT+30 continuous abstinence, varenicline nonabstainers who continued: main p7 and supp 2 p10 give n = 42; eFigure 2 (supp 2 p15) gives 0/77, the continuation group used in all analyses (42 re-randomized + 35 assigned).
rows.evidence: Main PDF p6-7 (text, Figure 2 rendered); supplement 2 p9-10 (text), p15 eFigure 2 (rendered). Card C008 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: 42 counts only the re-randomized continuers; the analysis denominator is 77. The estimate (0%) is the same either way; labeling error. Minor.

rows.R: Main p7 (and supp 2 p10): at 6 months 'only the CNRT patch increase (3%) and varenicline dosage increase (2%) provided benefit over continuation (0%)'. eFigure 3 (supp 2 p16) and supp p11: CNRT+ 6% (3/50) vs CNRT continuation 3% (3/90); RD 3% (eTable 9). The CNRT figures conflate an RD with an arm rate and misstate continuation as 0%.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p7 (text); supplement 2 p10-11 (text), p16 eFigure 3 (rendered), p33 eTable 9 (text). Card C009 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: 3/50=6%, 3/90=3.3%; RD 3% (0-6%), probability 96%. The summary sentence is wrong for CNRT (continuation 3%, not 0%), though the RD and benefit probability are correct elsewhere. Secondary outcome; minor.

rows.R: Protocol Figure 2 (supp 1 p32), repeated in eFigure 1 (supp 2 p14): week-6 response '0.48, 0.38-0.58 ~Beta(193,210)' and '0.50, 0.40-0.60 ~Beta(785,869)'. These betas give 95% intervals 0.43-0.53 and 0.45-0.50 (mean 0.475 for the second), whereas the 8 week-12 boxes reproduce their stated intervals.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p31-34 (text); supplement 2 p5, p14 (text). Computed in R (qbeta). Card C010 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: R qbeta: Beta(193,210) 0.430-0.528; Beta(785,869) mean 0.475, 0.451-0.499; Beta(47.3,47.3) 0.400-0.600 and Beta(62.2,21.0) 0.650-0.834 reproduce. The simulation inputs for week-6 response are internally inconsistent, so it is unclear how much uncertainty the power simulations assumed. The effect on the stated power cannot be determined from the documents.

rows.R: Supp 2 p8: revised intercept prior 'Normal(mean = 0, variance = 10)', with odds 95% interval 3.07e-9 to 325,215,956. That interval corresponds to SD = 10 (variance 100); variance 10 (SD 3.16) gives 0.0020 to 492. The main text (p4) also writes the coefficient prior as N(mu=0, sigma=1000), i.e., SD notation.
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p7-8 (text); main PDF p4 (text). Computed in R. Card C011 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: R: exp(+/-1.96*10) = 3.07e-9 to 3.25e8; exp(+/-1.96*sqrt(10)) = 0.0020 to 491.8. The prior's variance or the illustrative interval is misstated. Either prior is diffuse for an intercept, so posterior results are unlikely to be affected; reporting of the prior is inexact.

rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p10-11 (text), p15 eFigure 2 (rendered), p33, p35 (text). Card C012 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Decimal-scale transcription errors in the narrative (values divided by 10, interval limits out of order). The tables and figures are internally consistent, so the correct values are recoverable; minor.

rows.R: Six-month continuous abstinence, phase 1 abstainers (CNRT 39% vs varenicline 40%): supp 2 p12 gives ARD 1.0% (-1.3% to 1.1%), probability 55%; eTable 11 (p35) gives 1% (-11% to 12%), 56%. The narrative interval is wrong (scale error), and the sign is ambiguous (CNRT minus varenicline would be about -1%).
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p12, p16 eFigure 3 (rendered), p35 eTable 11 (text). Card C013 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: A difference of 1 point with groups of 54 and 88 cannot have a 95% interval of width 2.4 points; eTable 11's -11 to 12 is plausible. Secondary descriptive outcome; minor.

rows.R: eFigure 1 caption (supp 2 p14) describes CNRT+ as two 21-mg patches plus a 4-mg lozenge; eTables 1-2 captions, eFigures 2-3 captions (p15-18), the main text (p4, Figure 3 caption) and the protocol (p25) give two 21-mg patches (42 mg) plus 2-mg lozenges.
rows.evidence: Supplement 2 p14-18 (text); main PDF p4, p7, p8; supplement 1 p25 (text). Card read afterwards.
rows.rationale: A single caption gives a different lozenge dose for the augmented CNRT arm; all other locations agree on 2 mg. Intended meaning is clear; minor.

rows.R: Primary between-group difference in VAS change: abstract (p1), Results (p7), Table 2 (p6) and eTable 1 (supp 3 p2) give -0.3 (-0.27), consistent with placebo minus krill (-20.2 - (-19.9)); Key Points (p2) gives +0.30 with the same CI (-6.9 to 6.4). The direction convention is not defined anywhere.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1, p2, p6 Table 2 (rendered), p7; supplement 3 p2 eTable 1 (rendered). Card C001 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Arithmetic: -20.2-(-19.9)=-0.3; -20.21-(-19.93)=-0.28. Sign differs in Key Points; the magnitude is trivial and the CI and P are identical, so interpretation is unaffected. Undefined contrast direction (placebo minus krill, opposite to usual) adds ambiguity.

rows.evidence: Main PDF p2-3, p9 (text). Card C002 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: 5 mg per g = 0.005 = 0.5%. Typographic decimal error; minor.

rows.R: Protocol (supp 1 p8): primary VAS item 'how would you rate your pain today?'. Report (p3, Table 1 footnote b): knee pain VAS over the past 7 days.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p6, p8 (text); main PDF p3, p5 (text). Card C003 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Recall period of the primary outcome differs (today vs past 7 days). This changes the construct measured, even if the scale is the same.

rows.R: Methods (p4): ICOAP item scores 0-4 (never to very often); constant 0-20, intermittent 0-24, total 0-44. Table 1 footnote g (p5): 5 constant and 8 intermittent questions with responses 'not at all' to 'extremely'. 8 x 4 = 32, not 24 (ICOAP has 6 intermittent items), and total would be 52.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p4, p5 Table 1 footnote g, p6 (text). Card C004 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Arithmetic: 5x4=20, 6x4=24, total 44; 8x4=32. The footnote's item count and response labels conflict with the stated ranges; the rescaled 0-100 scores are unaffected if the ranges in Methods were used. Post hoc outcome; minor.

rows.R: Protocol (supp 1 p12): 10-mm VAS difference with SD 25.5 (12-week placebo change -15.5 +/- 25.5), 90% power, 234 needed, 260 with 10% loss; effusion: 96% power for a 20% difference in effusion area (mean 2.24 cm2, SD of change 1.35). Report (p4): SD 23.8 and a 4.5-mL change in effusion-synovitis volume, 130 per group, 90% power.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p2, p12 (text); main PDF p4 (text). Computed in R. Card C005 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: R power.t.test: delta 10, SD 25.5, 90% power needs 276 total (not 234); SD 23.8 with 130/group gives 92%. The report's assumptions (SD, effusion metric and effect size) differ from the plan's; the sample size is the same.

rows.R: Protocol (supp 1 p12) and SAP excerpt (supp 2 lines 5-7): linear regression of change scores, univariate and multivariable if groups unbalanced. Report (p4, p7): linear mixed model with treatment, month and treatment x month, random intercepts for participant and site, random slope for month, adjusting for imbalanced baseline values.
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p12; supplement 2 p1 (text); main PDF p4, p7 (text). Card C006 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Primary analysis model changed from a single-time-point linear regression to a longitudinal mixed model using all visits. Not disclosed as a change.

rows.R: Protocol and SAP (supp 1 p12; supp 2 lines 8-9): per-protocol analyses in participants consuming >=80% of capsules. Not reported; supp 3 eTable 1 gives age-adjusted and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses, and adherence is described (95% took >=80%).
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p12; supplement 2 p1; main PDF p4, p6-7; supplement 3 p2-3 (rendered/text). Card C007 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Planned per-protocol analysis not reported. The planned propensity-weighting approach to missing data was also replaced by age adjustment and multiple imputation (related difference).

rows.R: Under the placebo-minus-krill convention that reproduces other rows (e.g., VAS -20.2-(-19.9)=-0.3; ICOAP intermittent 1.5; function week 4 -19): ICOAP total (Table 2) -8.2-(-9.9)=1.7 vs printed 2.05; WOMAC weight-bearing week 4 (supp 3 p5) -103-(-84)=-19 vs printed 3 (the arm changes duplicate the function row); hsCRP week 12 (p6) 0.24-(-0.53)=0.77 vs printed 0.07.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p6 Table 2 (rendered); supplement 3 p5-6 eTable 4 (rendered); main p4, p7 methods. Card C008 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: In a single mixed model, the between-group difference in change equals the difference of the arm-specific changes (linear combinations of the same coefficients), up to rounding. Three rows violate this beyond rounding; the weight-bearing week-4 arm values are evidently copied from the function row, and hsCRP week 12 shows the glucose contrast (0.07). Secondary/post hoc outcomes; none changes a conclusion, but extracted values would be wrong.

rows.R: Table 3 (p8) vs eTable 7 (supp 3 p10-11): cough krill 2/placebo 0 vs 0/2; nasopharyngitis 2/1 vs 1/2; GERD 1/3 vs 3/1; abdominal discomfort 0/3 vs 3/0; diarrhea 2/1 vs 1/2; pain in extremity 1/6 vs 1/5 (abstract 1/5). eTable 7 subrows sum to the class totals (respiratory 9/16; GI 13/6), so Table 3 subrows are attributed to the wrong arm.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p1, p8 Table 3 (rendered); supplement 3 p10-11 eTable 7 (rendered, rows summed). Card C009 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: eTable 7 sums: respiratory krill 1+1+1+1+1+4=9, placebo 1+1+2+1+1+2+1+1+1+4+1=16; GI krill 3+1+1+1+1+3+1+1+1=13, placebo 2+1+1+1+1=6, matching the class totals in Table 3. Several specific adverse events in the main table are reversed between arms, which would mislead extraction of harms.

rows.R: Table 3 (p8): 'any treatment-related serious adverse event' 0 and 0; footnote b and text: no SAEs related to treatment / all unrelated. eTable 8 (supp 3 p14) rates relationship as possible for most SAEs and probable for one krill oil SAE (transfusion-dependent anaemia), unlikely for two.
rows.evidence: Main PDF p8 Table 3 and text (rendered); supplement 3 p14 eTable 8 (rendered). Card C010 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: SAE counts reconcile (krill 9, placebo 6), but the relatedness classification does not: eTable 8 lists 1 probable and several possible events in each arm, contradicting 'none related'. Safety attribution in the main text is therefore unreliable.

rows.R: Protocol (supp 1 p12): 260 participants give 96% power to detect a 20% difference in effusion size (mean 2.24 cm2, SD of change 1.35). A two-sample t calculation gives about 72% (117 per group) or 76% (130 per group). The primary power statement also does not reproduce (SD 25.5 requires 276 for 90% power, not 234).
rows.evidence: Supplement 1 p2, p12 (text); supplement 2 p1. Computed in R. Card C011 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: R power.t.test(n=117, delta=0.448, sd=1.35)=0.715; n=130: 0.760; power.t.test(delta=10, sd=25.5, power=0.9) total n=275. Unstated assumptions (e.g., a different SD, baseline adjustment, or a 20% difference defined otherwise) could explain the numbers, so I cannot establish which input is wrong.

rows.R: eTable 4 (supp 3 p6): fasting glucose week-12 contrast 0.07 (-1.19 to 1.33) has exactly the interval of the hsCRP week-12 row; with arm CIs about 0.3 wide, a 2.5-wide contrast interval cannot be right. The WOMAC total week-24 interval being narrower than a root-sum-of-squares of arm intervals is not by itself an error, since arm changes share model coefficients.
rows.evidence: Supplement 3 p5-6 eTable 4 (rendered); main PDF p6 Table 2 (rendered), p4, p7 (methods). Card C012 read afterwards; I accept only the glucose element.
rows.rationale: The glucose week-12 row reproduces hsCRP's interval verbatim, a copy error (glucose week 24: 0.04, -0.23 to 0.30, width consistent with arm intervals). For WOMAC, arm changes in a treatment x month mixed model are positively correlated through the common month effect, so the difference CI can be narrower than the RSS rule; no error shown there.

rows.R: eTable 5 (supp 3 p8), WORMS effusion change: percentages are identical in both arms and match pooled proportions (e.g., smaller by 1 unit 26/216 = 12.0%; no change 155/216 = 72%), not arm-specific ones (10/107 = 9.3%; 16/109 = 14.7%; 80/107 = 74.8%; 75/109 = 68.8%).
rows.evidence: Supplement 3 p8 eTable 5 (rendered). Card C013 read afterwards.
rows.rationale: Arithmetic: krill 2+10+80+12+3=107; placebo 2+16+75+13+3=109; pooled 4/216=1.9%, 26/216=12.0%, 155/216=71.8%, 25/216=11.6%, 6/216=2.8%. Counts are correct; percentages are pooled totals shown under each arm. Minor.
